planner.question: Can a precisely defined Gaussian/counting proof system separate finite completeness from efficient certificate discovery?
planner.strategy: Define and check a hybrid calculus that simulates resolution.
planner.alternative: Analyze exact redundant parity-cut separation, rank algorithm and uniform-point hardness.
planner.stop_rule: Do not charge exact cut separation as polynomial or infer unrestricted separation from oracle hardness.
literature_leads: Puchert and Tillmann, arXiv:2004.03387 (known general redundant parity-check separation hardness).
Garey and Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979), X3C SP2.

construct.claim: The specified fixed-variable Gaussian-to-counting calculus is sound and refutation complete with polynomial-time proof checking.
construct.scope: Explicit Boolean variables, parity rows and normalized clauses, exact integer sum/division, no extension variables.
construct.derivation: Parity cuts exclude forbidden patterns; expand source rows to clauses; simulate each non-tautological resolution step using Boolean bounds and rounding.
unresolved_steps: Polynomial proof size and uniform discovery on arbitrary inputs.
candidate_tests: All mixed three-variable fixtures, actual proof replay and malformed certificates.

alternative.claim: Exact redundant affine parity-cut separation is rank-parameterized and NP-complete even on consistent systems at uniform rational points.
alternative.scope: XOR combinations of supplied parity rows, arbitrary forbidden pattern; point need not satisfy initial cuts.
alternative.derivation: Optimize forbidden pattern by nearest bits plus minimum parity-changing flip; reduce X3C to odd RHS affine coset sparse row search.
unresolved_steps: Sufficient incomplete cut policies with universal polynomial bounds.
candidate_tests: Rational grid exhaustive cuts and 256 X3C subfamilies.

objections: Refutation completeness is not polynomial boundedness.
Exact separation hardness does not cover approximate or selective cut discovery.
Uniform-point reduction does not require initial-cut feasibility.
counterexample_candidates: Consistent incidence systems without exact cover; even-row cuts cannot violate at the selected point.
critic.equivalence_audit: Exact forbidden-pattern cuts and resolution simulation; X3C reduction both directions.
critic.barrier_audit: Known general RPC hardness acknowledged; no proof of P!=NP.
